value.body: A two-year master's degree covering crime-scene management, forensic chemistry and toxicology, biology and DNA, fingerprints, questioned documents, ballistics and digital forensics, with lab work and often a lab internship. It is the usual qualification for scientific posts in forensic labs.

items.label: Main entrances
items.note: NFAT is the National Forensic Sciences University's own test

value.title: How you get in
value.body: A bachelor's in science (forensic science, chemistry, life sciences and similar), and at some universities also medicine, pharmacy or engineering, usually with a minimum percentage. Admission is through NFAT for the National Forensic Sciences University, CUET-PG, or a state or university test.

value.title: At a glance
items: Many forensic lab posts specify a master's in forensic science or a related science.
Students usually specialise in one division (DNA, toxicology, documents, digital forensics).
Forensic Science is a UGC-NET subject, which leads to lectureship or JRF.
